output.brief: Most of what you were told is not supported. The single potassium flag on Analyzer B (11 Nov, Level 2) looks like a one-off: 182 of 182 scheduled QC runs were completed on time, the only failure in the period was that one, the repeat passed, and the Level 2 average did not move after the reagent lot change. Analyzer B and Analyzer A agree closely on the 20 re-runs and the 23 held samples, and Ward 6's high results were split evenly between the two analyzers, so the analyzers are not the likely cause of Ward 6's high potassiums. The Ward 6 tube outage, which made samples take longer to reach the lab, is the more likely contributor, though that link is an association not yet proven. Staffing did not cause missed QC. I am not sure what caused the single flag; a sampling glitch is possible but unproven. Do not widen the limits or recall about 2,900 results; both are unjustified and the recall would mean recollecting every patient. Do not sign off "isolated, no amendments" yet. Next: keep Analyzer B on hold until the director reviews the flag, run extra Level 2 checks after return, and fix the Ward 6 sample transport delay.
